attributes.body_ja:
「当（あ）たり」は、数字（すうじ）や助数詞（じょすうし）のあとに付（つ）く接尾語（せつびご）として使（つか）われます。「(A) ごとに」と同（おな）じような意味（いみ）を持（も）っていて、単位（たんい）ごとの数（かず）や量（りょう）を表（あらわ）します。例（れい）を見（み）てみましょう。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「当（あ）たり」はもともと、「触（ふ）れる」や「ぶつかる」などの意味（いみ）を持（も）つ名詞（めいし）ですが、接尾語（せつびご）の「当（あ）たり」は、「に対（たい）して」と同（おな）じようなニュアンスを持（も）ちます。どちらも「(A) に (B) が相当（そうとう）する」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
When attached to the end of numbers or counters, the noun 当（あ）たり 'to hit' will be used as a suffix. In these cases, the meaning is usually translated as 'per (A)', or 'each (A)'. Let's take a look at some examples.

Fun Fact

While the literal meaning of 当（あ）たり is 'to meet' (as in 'to come into physical contact with'), as a suffix, 当（あ）たり has a nuance that is similar to に対（たい）して 'to be in relation to'. This similarity can be seen in the following:

(A) 当（あ）たり (B) - Regarding (A), (B) equates to it.

(A) に対（たい）して (B) - Regarding (A), (B) equates to it.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: Both express the idea of 'each', but with different nuance and usage. ～ずつ attaches to quantity expressions like numbers or 少し to mean 'each' or 'at a time', e.g. 一つずつください 'Give me one of each.' or ちょっとずつよくなってきた 'It's gotten better a little at a time.' 当たり also attaches to Number + Counter, but means 'per' or 'apiece', e.g. １個当たり５００円です 'They're 500 yen apiece.'

first_relatable.title: ～ずつ
first_relatable.meaning: One at a time, Per, Each, Gradually

attributes.body: Both phrases derive from 当たる, but are used in very different ways. に当たる means 'corresponds to' and often functions as a more formal, indirect way of saying 'is', e.g. '父親に当たる人' ('a person who is [lit. corresponds to] their father'). 当たり is used after number + counter expressions to mean 'per' or 'apiece', e.g. '１個当たり１００円' ('100 yen apiece').

first_relatable.title: に当たる
first_relatable.meaning: Correspond to, Amounts to, Equals to, Is appropriate

attributes.body: 当たり and それぞれ can both convey a sense of 'each', but their nuances are different. 当たり attaches to numbers to mean 'each' in the sense of 'apiece', e.g. １個当たり１００円 ('100 yen each' / '100 yen apiece'). In contrast, それぞれ means 'each' in the sense of 'to each their own', e.g. 人はそれぞれ個性がある ('People each have unique traits').
